data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Galya is derived from the Hebrew word 'gal' meaning 'witness'. Galya is a Biblical name that symbolizes God's witness at Calvary. In the New Testament, Galya refers to the wife of King Herod Agrippa I. The name Galya carries the meaning “God's Calvarian Witness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Galya usually hope their child will grow to embody god's calvarian witness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
